papers.title: Molybdenum-driven dual redox regulation to improve capacity and stability of manganese-based cation-disordered rock-salt cathodes
papers.abstract: Mn-based Li-excess cation-disordered rocksalt (DRX) cathodes have garnered great attention for their flexibility in composition regulation and high capacity stemming from the cooperative involvement of cationic transition metal (TM) and anionic oxygen redox. Whereas, the reported DRXs to date suffer from significant capacity fading with limited cycle lifetime. A comprehensive understanding the local structure evolution in disordered lattice structure and regulating the distinct redox processes is critical to balance the high capacity and cyclability in DRXs. Herein, we incorporate a trace amount of redox-active Mo into bulk phase to regulate transition-metal and oxygen dual redox chemistry. By combining atomic-resolution microscopy and synchrotron X-ray techniques, we reveal that Mo dopants function as an electronic and structural regulator, which not only contributes to the charge compensation to cationic and anionic redox process, but also stabilizes lattice oxygen with improved local structural adaptability. The optimized Mo-doped DRX cathode achieves a high initial discharge capacity of 319.9 mAh g −1 at 10 mA g −1 (vs. 241.8 mAh g −1 for the pristine electrode), and maintains 119.4 mAh g −1 after 60 cycles. This work provides a new strategy to stabilize dual redox processes via trace redox-active doping, facilitating the development of high-performance oxygen-redox DRX cathodes.

papers.title: Where should straw return be promoted? Spatial zoning of management suitability based on C/N ratio optimization in Northeast China
papers.abstract: CONTEXT Straw return is widely promoted as a key conservation practice in the black soil region of Northeast China, yet its effects on crop yield, soil nutrients, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are highly variable across locations and management contexts. This heterogeneity has hindered the transition from uniform promotion to spatially targeted management strategies. OBJECTIVE This study aims to quantify the overall effects of straw return on soil–crop–emission indicators, identify the key drivers and causal pathways governing yield and GHG responses, determine the optimal soil C/N ratio window for synergistic yield gain and GHG mitigation, and translate this window into spatially explicit management suitability zones under future climate scenarios. METHODS An integrated framework was developed, coupling meta-analysis of 180 paired field observations, random forest, structural equation modeling (SEM), NSGA-II multi-objective optimization, and remote sensing–GIS spatial mapping. Three complementary nonlinear detection methods with bootstrap uncertainty quantification were employed to delineate C/N ratio thresholds. RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS Meta-analysis revealed that straw return significantly increased available phosphorus (17.7%), available potassium (12.9%), total nitrogen (4.4%), soil organic carbon (9.5%), and crop yield (6.5%). GHG emission responses were highly heterogeneous: N₂O showed a non-significant increase, while CH₄ increased substantially (64.8%, p < 0.001), with both indicators exhibiting high spatial variability across provinces. Total nitrogen was the dominant driver of yield response, whereas soil organic carbon was the dominant driver of GHG response; management practices exerted stronger control on GHG emissions than on yield. SEM identified a cascading pathway from climate through soil carbon and nitrogen pools and C/N ratio to yield response, with C/N ratio as the key mediator. Three complementary threshold detection methods consistently delineated an optimal C/N management range of 12.53–14.65. NSGA-II optimization yielded a knee-point management strategy (N at approximately 205.35 kg ha −1 , straw at approximately 9838 kg ha −1 ). Spatial zoning revealed 46.7% of cropland in Heilongjiang Province as a structural-optimization priority zone, and optimized strategies in southern low-latitude areas remained robust under SSP1–2.6, SSP2–4.5, and SSP5–8.5 scenarios. SIGNIFICANCE These findings demonstrate that spatially differentiated straw management guided by C/N ratio optimization can balance food security and GHG mitigation goals more effectively than uniform recommendations. The framework provides a quantitative scientific basis and a spatially explicit decision-support tool for transitioning straw return policy from uniform promotion to precision management tailored to local soil stoichiometric conditions.

papers.title: Full-vectorial physics-informed neural operator for forward and inverse waveguide modeling
papers.abstract: Abstract In this work, we tailor Physics-Informed Neural Operators for full-vectorial modal analysis of optical waveguides. We develop a two-headed neural operator, conditioned on coordinate inputs alongside spatial material profiles and operational parameters. This enables a unified framework that simultaneously predicts the effective indices and the corresponding electromagnetic field distributions while preserving the discretization invariance of neural operators. To ensure stable training, we employ a normalized eigenvalue prediction strategy, enforced by construction and complemented by a short-lived biasing term, yielding accurate and robust predictions. Moreover, the differentiable nature of the proposed framework naturally supports inverse design, allowing figures of merit like dispersion to be exactly calculated and optimized. The forward model achieves 1–2% relative errors compared against analytic solutions and standard numerical benchmarks, while offering up to a 29-fold speedup when evaluated on a GPU. This high forward-model accuracy also translates to notable agreement in the dispersion curves compared to the numerical references, capturing both magnitude and spectral trends across the considered parameter ranges.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Based Predictive Modeling and Simulation for Critical Infrastructure Asset Management in Saudi Arabia
papers.abstract: In Saudi Arabia critical infrastructure is growing and at the same time becoming more connected, equipped with a greater number of sensors, and operationally interdependent. Because of these features there arises an asset-management problem which cannot be properly solved by means of periodic inspections, isolated condition monitoring or static risk registers. This article critically looks at the way in which digital twin-based predictive modelling and simulation can assist with making decisions throughout the lifecycle of assets in the energy, water, transport, industrial and built-environment sectors. Evidence from between 2020 and 2025 is combined in a structured integrative review, with a focus on digital-twin architecture, data synchronisation, predictive maintenance, uncertainty-aware simulation, interoperability, cyber-physical trust and decision governance. The literature shows that value is not derived simply from visualisation but comes from keeping a continuously updated representation in which operational data constrain the models, the models forecast degradation, and simulations are used to test maintenance or recovery options before any actual intervention takes place. Hybrid approaches that combine physics-based models with machine learning seem especially appropriate for safety-critical assets since they are able to retain engineering meaning while making use of high-frequency data. Yet implementation is still limited by fragmented asset information, inconsistent semantics, a lack of validation across different operating conditions, exposure to cyberattacks, uncertainty regarding the transferability of models and poor integration with existing enterprise asset-management workflows. For Saudi Arabia a step-by-step approach is suggested in which data foundations, model fidelity, human supervision and interoperable governance all develop together. The review ends by stating that digital twins should be seen as decision infrastructure rather than as software replicas, and their performance should be measured in terms of the number of failures avoided, the improvement in maintenance timing, resilience, lifecycle cost and the quality of decisions that can be audited.

papers.title: Physics‐Guided Active Learning Enables Energy‐Filtering Flexible Thermoelectric Composites for Self‐Powered Wound Bioelectronics
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermoelectric stimulation offers a self‐powered intervention for accelerated wound healing by converting physiological thermal gradients into sustained micro‐electric fields. However, the development of flexible thermoelectric materials is constrained by the coupled dependence of electrical conductivity and the Seebeck coefficient, which empirical screening alone is inefficient for exploring the large number of possible interfaces. We developed a small‐data, literature‐derived, physics‐guided screening and design framework that integrates Bayesian optimization with eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) regression and subsequent experimental validation. Using 18 physics‐informed descriptors selected by recursive feature elimination, the framework predicts interfacial energy barriers within the literature‐derived data domain with a test R 2 of 0.87, enabling targeted barrier engineering that partially decouples the thermoelectric parameters. The model and practical screening criteria were used to select five composite systems for synthesis and experimental evaluation, supporting the applicability of the algorithm. Among the experimentally validated systems, poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene): poly(styrene sulfonate)/eutectic gallium‐indium (PEDOT:PSS/EGaIn) flexible composite exhibited a measured interfacial energy barrier of 0.24 eV, close to the predicted effective filtering range, and achieved a Seebeck coefficient of 40.0 µV K −1 . Under a mild physiological‐to‐ambient temperature gradient of 25 K, the flexible thermoelectric device generated an open‐circuit voltage of 8.80 mV. In the scratch assay, the stimulated group showed 34.5% closure compared with 13.9% in the untreated control. In the rat wound model, the thermoelectric group reached near‐complete closure approximately two days earlier than the sham and untreated groups. This data‐driven approach provides a physical framework for screening energy‐filtering composites and evaluating their potential in self‐powered bioelectronic therapeutics.

papers.title: Effect of Low-Level Laser Therapy on Stability of Dental Implants in D3 and D4 Bone Quality: A Split-Mouth Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Achieving predictable implant stability in low-density maxillary bone (D3-D4) remains clinically challenging because reduced bone density is associated with greater early loss of stability and an increased risk of implant failure. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has been proposed to enhance osseointegration; however, clinical evidence regarding its effect on implant stability in low-density bone remains limited and inconsistent. The aim of this study is to evaluate the effect of 940-nm diode laser photobiomodulation (PBM) on implant stability during early healing in low-density maxillary bone (D3-D4). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This split-mouth, randomized controlled clinical trial included medically healthy adults who required bilateral maxillary implants. A total of 40 implants were placed in 10 participants using a guided flapless protocol. Test sites received 940-nm diode laser PBM immediately after implant placement and at 2-week intervals for 2 months, while contralateral sites served as controls. Implant stability was measured using resonance frequency analysis and expressed as implant stability quotient (ISQ) at baseline (T0), 2 months (T1), and 3 months (T2). Data was analyzed using linear mixed-effects model as primary analysis and two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance as supportive. RESULTS: In the primary mixed-effects analysis, implant stability did not differ significantly between the PBM and control groups at baseline (estimated mean difference [PBM control], -2.45 ISQ; P = 0.341). At 2 months, PBM-treated implants demonstrated significantly higher estimated stability than control implants (mean difference, 6.30 ISQ; 95% CI, 1.21-11.39; P = 0.016). At 3 months, no significant between-group difference was observed (mean difference, 0.40 ISQ; P = 0.878). The linear mixed-effects model demonstrated a significant time × treatment interaction (P = 0.042), indicating that implant-stability trajectories differed between the groups over time. The complete-case repeated-measures ANOVA yielded a consistent significant time × treatment interaction (P = 0.007). No adverse effects related to PBM were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Photobiomodulation using a 940-nm diode laser enhanced early implant stability and reduced the magnitude of the stability dip in D3-D4 maxillary bone without affecting final implant stability after 3 months. PBM may represent a safe adjunctive approach to support early osseointegration in low-density bone.

papers.title: Focal Osteoporosis Around Dental Implants: Indicator of Success or Sign of Failure? A Comprehensive Review of Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Clinical Implications
papers.abstract: Abstract Statement of problem: Localized radiographic radiolucency or reduced bone density around dental implants is sometimes described as “focal osteoporosis”. The clinical significance of this finding remains unclear and may be misinterpreted as implant failure. Purpose: This review aims to evaluate whether focal osteoporosis around dental implants represents a transient physiologic bone remodeling phenomenon compatible with success or a pathological process indicating failure. Materials and Methods: A narrative review of peer-reviewed literature was conducted focusing on peri-implant bone remodeling, stress shielding, systemic osteoporosis, peri-implant radiographic interpretation, and osseointegration biology. Results: Focal reduction in bone density around implants may occur as part of adaptive remodeling following load application. When associated with maintained implant stability, absence of inflammation, and stable marginal bone levels, it does not indicate failure. However, progressive radiolucency combined with mobility or inflammatory signs suggests loss of osseointegration and failure. Conclusions: Focal osteoporosis is not inherently synonymous with implant failure. Clinical correlation, longitudinal radiographic assessment, and stability testing are essential before determining prognosis. Clinical Implications: Proper differentiation between physiologic remodeling and pathological bone loss prevents unnecessary implant removal and supports evidence-based decision-making.

papers.title: 'The Disappearing Implant': Magnesium-Based Biodegradable Fixation in Oral Surgery- A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Abstract Conventional titanium plates and screws remain the primary choice for maxillofacial bone fixation because they are strong, reliable, and predictable over time. However, since they remain in the body permanently, they sometimes need to be removed later and can cause issues such as stress shielding, being felt beneath the skin, imaging problems, and interference with bone growth. Magnesium-based biodegradable fixation systems are a promising new option. They offer the strength of metal devices but gradually break down after the bone heals. Magnesium alloys are less stiff than titanium, which may help reduce problems such as stiffness mismatch and stress shielding, while still providing sufficient support during healing. As magnesium breaks down in the body, it corrodes, producing magnesium ions, corrosion products, hydroxide ions, and hydrogen gas. If magnesium ions are released in a controlled way, they may help bone and blood vessel growth. Early studies in both labs and clinics have shown promising results from the use of magnesium alloys in jaw and facial bone surgeries. Still, there are challenges, such as rapid or uneven breakdown, buildup of hydrogen gas, early loss of strength, device failure, and insufficient long-term clinical data. Researchers are now exploring ways to improve these materials, such as changing the surface, adjusting the alloy mix, and tailoring devices to each patient. Magnesium-based biodegradable fixation systems are a promising new option for fixing facial and jaw bones. They can provide strong support initially and then gradually dissolve, potentially eliminating the need for routine hardware removal. However, there is not yet enough evidence to fully replace titanium, especially in areas that bear heavy loads. More research is needed to better control how these materials break down, reduce hydrogen gas, improve the alloy and its surface, and run larger clinical trials. As materials and manufacturing improve, magnesium-based systems could become a standard choice for some facial bone surgeries. This review examines how magnesium-based biodegradable fixation systems operate in oral and maxillofacial surgery. It focuses on their mechanical and biological properties, how they break down, their clinical use, benefits, drawbacks, when they should or should not be used, how they degrade, what current research shows, and what the future might hold. Keywords: Magnesium; Biodegradable magnesium alloys; Bioresorbable fixation; Oral surgery; Magnesium implants; Biodegradable plates.

papers.title: MENINGKATKAN LITERASI DAN NUMERISASI DEMI MENUNJANG PEMBELAJARAN DI KURIKULUM MERDEKA MELALUI PROGRAM BIMBINGAN BELAJAR KKN DI DESA BALONGMASIN
papers.abstract: Peningkatan literasi dan numerasi merupakan kompetensi dasar yang menjadi fokus Kurikulum Merdeka dalam mencetak generasi yang kreatif, kritis, dan mandiri. Namun, di Desa Balongmasin, banyak siswa sekolah dasar masih menghadapi keterbatasan dalam membaca, menulis, dan berhitung, yang dapat menghambat pencapaian kompetensi akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kemampuan literasi dan numerasi siswa melalui program bimbingan belajar yang dilaksanakan oleh mahasiswa KKN dengan pendekatan active learning, intervensi individual, dan metode kreatif berbasis proyek. Subjek penelitian terdiri dari 10 responden yang dipilih secara purposive sampling berdasarkan keterbatasan kemampuan awal mereka. Instrumen penelitian meliputi tes pretest-posttest, observasi, dan questionnaire untuk menilai perkembangan kemampuan dan partisipasi siswa. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan adanya peningkatan signifikan pada seluruh responden, dengan skor literasi meningkat antara 34,5% hingga 60,9% dan numerasi meningkat antara 68% hingga 95,3%. Peningkatan ini mencerminkan efektivitas pendekatan pembelajaran yang kontekstual, interaktif, dan diferensiasi individual dalam memperkuat kompetensi dasar siswa. Program ini juga meningkatkan motivasi, keterlibatan, dan kepercayaan diri siswa, sekaligus memperkuat peran mahasiswa KKN dan dukungan keluarga dalam menciptakan ekosistem belajar yang inklusif dan berkelanjutan.
